Article Title: 'Lot of pressure on him, happened in just 2 hrs': Robert Vadra on son Raihan’s Bikaner exhibition row
Article Text:
Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, the son of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Robert Vadra, during his solo exhibition at Bikaner House, in New Delhi.

‘All 75 had to be taken down’

NEW DELHI: Businessman Robert Vadra has alleged that pressure was exerted on his son, artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, to remove photographs documenting recent protests in Delhi from his solo exhibition at Bikaner House, with the intervention coming just hours before the scheduled opening.Calling the episode shocking, Robert said the authorities had received the exhibition’s PDF a week in advance and had raised no objections until the final hours. He also praised Raihan for proceeding with the exhibition despite the removal of several photographs.“There was a lot of pressure on him to remove everything, and this happened just two hours before the opening of his exhibition. It was shocking because the authorities had received the PDF file a week in advance and had been informed about the exhibition,” Robert said.He said setting up an exhibition required considerable effort and that officials had visited the venue, seen the displays and raised no objections initially. However, the situation changed shortly before the opening, he alleged, without any explanation.“Despite this, I think he was brave enough to go ahead with the exhibition using whatever remained. As I said, I am proud of him. Everyone who had been invited attended the exhibition because this is also his profession,” he said.In a separate statement, Robert said Raihan had worked hard on the exhibition, which drew on photographs he took while documenting protests in the national capital.“I am very proud of my son, Raihan, for the hard work he puts in every time he takes up a subject that is relevant to what is happening around him,” he said.Robert said Raihan had attended the protests, keeping his friends in mind and considering the support students needed. He carried his camera to the demonstrations, captured photographs and expressions, and later decided to organise an exhibition on the subject.According to Robert, Raihan submitted a PDF of the proposed exhibition to Bikaner House officials about a week before the event. He alleged that the authorities did not raise concerns about the material at the time.However, in the final 24 hours, after Raihan and his team had spent considerable time setting up the exhibition, officials arrived to review the displays, Robert said. The commissioner of Bikaner House subsequently told them that certain displays would have to be removed.“When Raihan asked how many displays were an issue and offered to remove any that were considered controversial, he was told that all 75 had to be taken down,” Robert alleged.Robert also questioned the decision to remove the photographs, saying artistic expression should be allowed in a democracy. He pointed out that Bikaner House comes under the Rajasthan government.“If we believe in democracy, there is no point in mixing politics with the creative world. Everyone should be allowed to express themselves,” he said.The controversy centres on Raihan’s solo exhibition,, after he alleged that more than 70 photographs documenting recent youth-led protests in Delhi were removed shortly before the exhibition opened. Bikaner House has said certain photographs were inconsistent with its policy, which it said focuses on culture and wildlife, and that the removed images carried political messaging.
Article Summary: Businessman Robert Vadra has alleged that pressure was exerted on his son, artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, to remove photographs. The intervention came just hours before the scheduled opening of his solo exhibition at Bikaner House. Robert said the authorities had received the exhibition’s PDF a week in advance and had raised no objections until the final hours.

NEW DELHI: Bikaner House Management Society on Thursday said it had requested the removal of certain photographs from Raihan Vadra’s exhibition, ‘No Idea Is Final’, after finding them inconsistent with its policy.The statement came after Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venue’s management had asked him to remove photographs depicting youth movements in Delhi just hours before the exhibition’s scheduled opening at 7 pm.In a statement, the society said Bikaner House was a public cultural institution dedicated to promoting art and culture, and that exhibitions held at the venue must comply with its management policy."Certain photographs displayed as part of Mr Raihan Vadra’s exhibition, No Idea Is Final', at Bikaner House were found to be inconsistent with the policy of the Bikaner House Management Society. Article Title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order from a foreign court while the other moves an Indian court, Supreme Court has said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child and the ruling of the foreign court should not be automatically followed, though it must be accorded proper consideration.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.“This position rests on two foundations. The first is that once the court is seized of the matter, it exercises its parens patriae jurisdiction. That jurisdiction obliges it to consider and assess the matter for itself, through the lens of the child’s welfare. The second is that the decision in such cases turns not on the legal rights of the parties but on the welfare of the child. The same emphasis on welfare over legal entitlement runs through our statutes on custody and guardianship. They make clear that a person otherwise entitled to custody or guardianship need not be granted it if that would not be for the welfare of the child.There is thus no ambiguity in the fact that an order of a foreign court must yield to the welfare of the child,” the bench said.“Put differently, a court in this country, when exercising its jurisdiction, cannot blindly follow the order of a foreign court and act merely as an executing court,” the apex court bench said.SC said a parent’s disobedience of a foreign court order did not, by itself, require the Indian court to give automatic effect to that order and also that the paramountcy of the child’s welfare did not mean that the order of the foreign court had to be disregarded. “In deciding what the welfare of the child requires, the court must form its own independent judgement. In doing so, however, it must give proper weight to the order of the foreign court,” the bench said.SC passed the order while directing that a seven-year-old girl, a US citizen, who was brought to India by her mother in breach of a California custody order, return to US.A California court had in 2022 granted the couple joint custody of the child and specifically barred her removal from California without written consent or a court order. In violation of the ruling, the mother left for India with the child after two weeks, leading to the father starting legal proceedings against her in India.SC allowed the petition of the father, who approached the court through advocate Prabhjit Jauhar, against a Karnataka HC order dismissing his plea. After hearing both sides, it said the welfare of the child lay in her continuing to reside in US.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again.

Article Title: Raihan Vadra’s protest photos spark political row, Congress alleges censorship, BJP hits back - all you need to know
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra’s protest photos spark political row

Bikaner House says photographs were inconsistent with its policy

Raihan Vadra questions restrictions on political art

Priyanka Gandhi backs son, Robert Vadra says family will find another venue

Gehlot calls removal of photographs censorship

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BJP targets Gandhi family over exhibition row

NEW DELHI: The Bikaner House Management Society on Thursday defended its request to remove certain photographs from visual artist Raihan Vadra’s exhibition, saying they were “found to be inconsistent” with its policy, as the dispute over the removal of images documenting student protests and photographs of the national flag escalated into a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP.Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the administration asked him to remove 70 of the 105 photographs displayed at his exhibition, No Idea Is Final, in New Delhi. He questioned the restrictions on political expression at an art institution, while several Congress leaders criticised the decision as censorship. The BJP, meanwhile, accused the Gandhi family of using the controversy for political purposes.In a statement on Thursday, the Bikaner House Management Society said certain photographs displayed at the exhibition were found to be inconsistent with its policy and their removal was requested. It added that the photographs considered consistent with its policy continued to be displayed."Bikaner House is a public cultural institution dedicated to the promotion of art and culture.The exhibition and associated activities must comply with Bikaner House Management Society policy," the statement said.The clarification came a day after Vadra alleged that the administration had asked him to remove several photographs documenting protests in Delhi, including images of the national flag, ahead of the exhibition's scheduled opening on Wednesday evening.In an Instagram post on Wednesday, Vadra said, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi.Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."He said the exhibition would proceed with the remaining works and that he would consider another venue if necessary to display the complete collection of protest photographs.Speaking to PTI Videos, Vadra said he had been informed about potential objections to some photographs a day before the exhibition and had asked the management to communicate its concerns in writing."My show, 'No Idea Is Final', was supposed to start at 7 pm yesterday at Bikaner House. Twenty-four hours before the opening, I was approached by the Bikaner House management and told that some of the pictures might be objectionable or against their policy. I said that I did not believe they are, but I am happy to discuss the matter and asked them to get back to me in writing as to what are the objections," he said.According to Vadra, the management did not respond until the following morning, when its team inspected the exhibition. He said he was subsequently told to remove 70 of the 105 photographs."I did not hear from them till 11 am next day when their team came, saw the exhibit and left, they even complimented me on some of the photographs. Then, around 12.30 pm, we received a call from the deputy resident commissioner saying that you have to remove 70 of the 105 photographs in the exhibition because they are against the policy," he said.Vadra said he had already removed some photographs containing overtly political slogans after reviewing the venue's policy and was willing to discuss concerns over images featuring flags and political leaders.The management later insisted that the remaining photographs considered objectionable be removed, he alleged. Vadra said he asked officials to put their objections in writing, particularly regarding the photographs of the national flag."So, we took them down except two photographs of the Indian flag which also they asked me to remove. I said, 'But they are just pictures of the Indian flag. I do not think there is anything in your policy that says photographs of the Indian flag have to be removed'. At that point, I firmly told them to put their demand in writing if they wanted me to remove the photographs of the Indian flag," Vadra said.He alleged that although the management did not provide a written demand, officials removed one of the two photographs while he was away.Vadra questioned the restriction on political expression at an art institution, saying, "I mean, most art is political, right? You cannot function as an artistic institution and then say that political content is not allowed," he said.He also alleged that he had shared a layout of the exhibition with the management a week earlier, but was later told that officials had not been able to review it.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son on Thursday, expressing support for his decision to stand by his work.In a post on X, she wrote, "When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn't know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be."Robert Vadra also expressed pride in his son and said the family would find another venue if necessary.Speaking to ANI, he said, "I am very proud of Raihan. He has seen what the whole family goes through and has gone through, and what his father has gone through. So, he is a very strong person, a very strong-headed person. He will find another location, and we will do it at another location.”He said Raihan had attended the recent protests, documenting them through photographs before deciding to organise an exhibition on the subject. According to Robert Vadra, his son had submitted a PDF of the proposed exhibition to the Bikaner House authorities about a week in advance, but they had not raised concerns about its content.Robert Vadra also questioned whether the decision was linked to the Rajasthan government or resulted from other pressures, adding that his son would not be prevented from showcasing his work.Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot criticised the BJP government over the controversy, describing the removal of the photographs as an attack on artistic expression and democracy."Bikaner House is a property of the Rajasthan government. This means a young artist's creativity was stifled under the BJP government's watch, which is highly condemnable," Gehlot said in a statement.He alleged that the government was attempting to suppress images reflecting public dissent and demanded an explanation for the removal of the photographs."Suppressing the voice of artists is a direct attack on democracy. This is a clear example of censorship," Gehlot said.Gehlot also praised Vadra for refusing to remove the two photographs featuring the national flag.Congress leader Pawan Khera also questioned the restrictions placed on the exhibition, arguing that artists should be able to express themselves through their work.Speaking to ANI, Khera said, "Raihan Vadra is an artist. We can't understand why this government is against the expression of art by an artist. Every day we see examples of how this government is against the youth voicing their opinions using different mediums, including art," Khera said.The BJP hit back at the Congress over the controversy, with party spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia targeting the Gandhi family and alleging that it was using the episode to pursue its political ambitions.Speaking on the issue, Bhatia said, “Congress' psychophant leaders are saying that he is the future president of Congress. One defective product who has lost 99 elections has not been launched by Sonia mummy. Now Priyanka mummy's mission has come to launch Raihan."Further targeting the Congress leadership, Bhatia alleged that the family was willing to do anything to regain power."This fake Gandhi family wants power every time, and as soon as they are out of power, they will do anything. They can do anything for power. The law will prevail in the country, be it the defective product Rahul Gandhi or the future president of Congress, Raihan Vadra. Priyanka mummy is now on a new mission. After the launch of Rahul Gandhi, Raihan will be launched,” he added.
Article Summary: Bikaner House Management Society defended its request to remove certain photographs from visual artist Raihan Vadra’s exhibition. The dispute over the removal of images documenting student protests and photographs of the national flag escalated into a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP. Vadra alleged that the administration asked him to remove 70 of the 105 photographs displayed at his exhibition.

Article Title: 'Told them to give it to me in writing': Raihan Vadra recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down at Bikaner House exhibition
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of Tricolour

Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation

Dispute over photographs of the Tricolour

NEW DELHI: Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, has detailed his interactions with Bikaner House officials over the removal of photographs depicting youth protests in Delhi from his exhibition, alleging that the administration gave him only a few hours to comply with its objections.Speaking about the controversy, Raihan said his solo exhibition, titled No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at 7 pm, but the venue's management raised objections to some of the photographs shortly before the event.He alleged that officials subsequently insisted that all 70 images be removed, including photographs featuring the Indian national flag.Speaking to news agency ANI, Raihan said the Bikaner House management first contacted him 24 hours before the scheduled opening and told him that some images violated its policy. He said he asked the officials to identify the photographs and discuss their objections, but did not receive a response until the following day.He said the deputy resident commissioner later contacted him and instructed him to remove the photographs, which documented youth movements in Delhi over the preceding year.“I said, 'I shared the layout a week earlier; why didn't you bring it up earlier?' They said, 'We couldn't see the layout.'So I said, 'You still had 1 week to tell me you couldn't see the layout. I would have sent it; we could have had the discussion earlier. Now, in 4-5 hours, what am I going to do?'” Raihan said.Raihan said he asked the management to provide written explanations for the removal of individual photographs but did not receive them.He said the principal resident commissioner subsequently visited the exhibition at around 3 pm and reiterated the objections. According to Raihan, the official cited the venue's policy against political content.Raihan said he had already removed most photographs featuring political parties and leaders and was willing to replace any remaining images that violated the policy.“For the most part, I had removed imagery of political parties and of political leaders. Maybe there were a few photographs; I said, 'We could discuss. If they are against your policy, I'll replace them.' He said, 'No, none of these 70 images will be put up,'” he said.According to Raihan, the management issued a notice at 3.30 pm warning that the building would be sealed and the exhibition cancelled if the photographs were not removed by 5 pm.He said he initially complied by turning the framed photographs around so that only their backs were visible. However, he alleged that officials objected to this arrangement as well, prompting him to take the frames down and move them into storage.Raihan said he left two photographs featuring the Indian flag on display, arguing that they could not reasonably violate the venue's policy. He alleged that officials asked him to remove them but did not provide a written order when he requested one.“I said, 'This can't be against your policy. How can it be against your policy?' I said, 'Give it to me in writing that you want me to take down a picture of the Indian flag.' They didn't,” he said.Raihan added that he left the venue to change clothes and that officials removed one of the two photographs themselves. One image of the national flag remained on display, he said.In an earlier statement, Raihan had said he would not remove the photographs featuring the Tricolour and that the exhibition would proceed in a limited capacity while he looked for an alternative venue to display the complete collection.The controversy drew reactions from members of the Congress. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X, writing, “When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn’t know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be.”Robert Vadra also shared his son's statement, while Congress MP Karti Chidambaram criticised the Bikaner House administration's conduct.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera alleged that the removal of the photographs amounted to censorship.In a post on X, he said the works documented protests and questioned why images of demonstrations, including the national flag, had become objectionable.The exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at Bikaner House on Thursday evening.
Article Summary: Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of the Tricolour.Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation for the removal of the images. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X.

Article Title: ‘Finding a place to belong’: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of memoir
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi joins Instagram, shares first look of memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’

Memoir revisits childhood, Rajiv Gandhi and family tragedies

India edition faces publishing uncertainty

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Thursday and shared the first look of her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which is scheduled for release on November 10.In her first post on the social media platform, the 79-year-old Congress leader expressed gratitude while introducing the book to readers.“Hello everyone, I’m truly grateful to share this moment with you all; the first look of Belonging: A Journey of Love,” she wrote in the caption.“It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” the post added.The memoir traces Congress MP’s journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her relationship with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with India.The book recounts Sonia’s early years in Italy, her romance with Rajiv Gandhi while they were associated with Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband.Born in Italy, Sonia Gandhi was 19 when she met Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge, England, in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968.She went on to become the longest-serving president of the Congress party.Her memoir is expected to offer a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, alongside her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her life in India.Rahul Gandhi had earlier expressed excitement about the book. On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha wrote that he was proud his mother’s story would reach readers.“I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia,” Rahul Gandhi said.The memoir is scheduled to be published internationally by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of the Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group, on November 10. The announcement was made on August 18.However, the book’s publication in India has faced uncertainty following a disagreement between Penguin Random House India (PRHI) and the author’s representatives over editorial changes.Penguin India said the publication process had reached an “impasse over a particular issue” during its normal editorial review. The publisher said some proposed changes had been accepted, while in other instances it had accepted the author’s position, but an agreement could not be reached on one issue.Penguin India denied that external pressure had influenced the decision and declined to disclose details of the disagreement, citing contractual obligations and author confidentiality.The dispute triggered a political controversy, with Congress leaders alleging that pressure had been exerted to remove sections concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and China’s occupation of Indian territory during the Modi government.Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot described the episode as a “murder of democracy”.Penguin India rejected suggestions of external intervention, saying its review involved the usual editorial processes, including fact-checking and recommendations.Later, HarperCollins India had stepped in to publish the domestic edition, with the book expected to reach Indian readers on the same date as its international release.The status of the India edition had remained a point of contention following Penguin India’s exit from the deal.Former Congress president’s Instagram debut comes ahead of the memoir’s scheduled release, offering readers an early glimpse of the book and its account of her personal journey.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi joins Instagram, shares first look of memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’Memoir revisits childhood, Rajiv Gandhi and family tragedies.India edition faces publishing uncertainty following disagreement with Penguin Random House India.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Travis Kelce incident could trigger costly NFL punishment for Chargers defender after controversial on-field hit
Article Text:
Chargers defensive lineman faces possible five-figure bill after controversial hit involving Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Daiyan Henley faces scrutiny over tackle on Travis Kelce

Henley could face a fine of nearly $18,000

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL could impose a five-figure fine on Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley if the league determines that his tackle on Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce violated its ban on hip-drop tackles. The incident occurred during the Chiefs’ 22-6 win on October 18, when Kelce appeared to hurt his ankle and briefly left the game. He returned to finish the contest, but the tackle has drawn scrutiny because of the technique involved. No official ruling or fine had been announced in the report published by Heavy, leaving Henley’s potential punishment unresolved.Henley’s tackle came during Kansas City’s opening offensive drive. Video of the play circulated online, prompting criticism from Chiefs fans and analysts who believed the linebacker had used an illegal hip-drop technique. Kelce’s apparent ankle injury added to the concern, although he was able to return to the field.The NFL bans hip-drop tackles when a defender unweights himself, swivels his hips and drops onto a ball carrier’s legs. The technique can place significant stress on the lower body, which is why the league has targeted it through its player-safety rules. The key question is whether Henley’s movement met all the criteria for a violation, not simply whether Kelce was hurt.Officials may miss the details of a tackle during live action, but the league can review the footage after a game. That process gives the NFL a chance to assess plays that were not penalized on the field. Heavy reported that the league had not officially confirmed a review of Henley’s tackle, so any suggestion that a fine is imminent remains speculative.Kelce’s return offered some relief for Kansas City, but it does not settle the question of whether the tackle broke league rules. The NFL can assess a play based on its mechanics even when the player involved avoids a serious injury.The financial risk is significant even if the NFL ultimately treats the incident as a first-time violation. According to the league’s official website, a first offense involving an illegal hip-drop tackle carries a baseline fine of $17,911. A repeat violation can raise the amount to $23,882, putting Henley at risk of a costly penalty if the league rules against him.The league’s response could also draw attention because of the history of injuries associated with this type of tackle. In 2023, a similar tackling motion ended Baltimore Ravens tight end Mark Andrews’ season. Kelce avoided that outcome, returning after briefly heading to the sideline, but the play has renewed questions about how consistently defenders follow the NFL’s restrictions.Chiefs coach Andy Reid offered a reassuring update after the game, saying Kelce might be sore but would still “be ok.” That was encouraging news for Kansas City, which had already secured the win. The focus now shifts to whether the NFL considers Henley’s technique a punishable offense.For the Chargers, the incident adds another concern after a sixth consecutive loss. A fine would not change the result against Kansas City, but it would put an individual disciplinary issue alongside the team’s wider struggles. Until the league issues its findings, however, Henley remains at risk of a penalty rather than a player who has been officially fined.
Article Summary: Daiyan Henley could face a fine of nearly $18,000 for tackle on Travis Kelce. Kelce appeared to hurt his ankle but returned to finish the game. NFL bans hip- drop tackles when defender unweights himself, swivels his hips and drops onto a ball carrier’s legs.

Article Title: "We are grateful for Tom’s generous support”: How Tom Brady donated his $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to Best Buddies and other charities to help those in need
Article Text:

Tom Brady gave away his $170,000 Salem State speaking fee

Best Buddies already had a strong relationship with Tom Brady

Tom Brady earned $170,000 for a one-hour speaking appearance at Salem State University in May 2015. But the former New England Patriots quarterback reportedly gave away the entire fee, sending $50,000 to Best Buddies and the rest to other charities. The donation came during a difficult stretch in his NFL career, with the Deflategate controversy dominating headlines and a four-game suspension hanging over him.The event attracted around 4,000 people, but Brady’s decision to donate the money gave the appearance another dimension. Here is how the payment, the charity contribution and his existing relationship with Best Buddies came together.Salem State University confirmed on June 16, 2015, that its nonprofit foundation had paid Brady $170,000 for his appearance at the school’s annual speaker series on May 7. Also, Boston Globe reported that Brady had donated the fee to charity, citing information from Best Buddies.According to the report, Best Buddies received $50,000, while other charities shared the remaining $120,000. The organization did not identify the other recipients in its announcement.Anthony Kennedy Shriver, Best Buddies’ founder and chairman, confirmed the contribution in a statement to The Boston Globe.“We are grateful for Tom’s generous support over the years,” Shriver said.The payment also raised questions about the cost of bringing a celebrity speaker to a public university. Salem State said ticket sales and corporate sponsorships covered Brady’s fee. The foundation made a profit of about $40,000 from the event, according to the university.Around 4,000 people attended the appearance. Tickets ranged from $20 to $100, with students paying $15, according to an Associated Press report published by CBS Boston on June 17, 2015.Brady also faced questions about Deflategate during the event. Speaking with television reporter Jim Gray at Salem State on May 7, he addressed the NFL investigation but declined to offer a detailed response to its findings.“I don’t really have any reaction [to the Wells Report]. It has only been 30 hours. I’ve not had much time to digest it,” Brady said during the Salem State appearance.His donation came as the NFL prepared to enforce a four-game suspension over the controversy. Brady appealed the punishment, setting up a dispute with commissioner Roger Goodell.The $50,000 contribution continued Brady’s support for Best Buddies, a nonprofit that promotes friendships and opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.Brady had helped the organization raise money through an annual charity football game at Harvard Stadium. The event brought together celebrities and children to support its work.The 2015 game took place at the end of May, just weeks after his Salem State appearance. Some fans wore “Free Brady” shirts at the fundraiser while the quarterback challenged his suspension.That existing relationship helps explain why Best Buddies featured prominently in the donation announcement. However, the organization’s statement did not say how Brady divided the remaining $120,000 among other charities.The Salem State appearance also had a financial benefit for the university. The foundation used ticket sales and corporate sponsorships to cover the speaking fee and other event expenses, and the school reported a profit rather than a loss.Brady’s donation therefore involved more than one charitable contribution. He gave Best Buddies $50,000, directed the rest of his speaking fee to other charities and continued supporting an organization with which he had an established fundraising relationship. The available reports confirm those details, although they do not provide a complete list of the other recipients.
Article Summary: Tom Brady earned $170,000 for a one-hour speaking appearance at Salem State University in May 2015. But the former New England Patriots quarterback reportedly gave away the entire fee, sending $50,000 to Best Buddies and the rest to other charities. The donation came during a difficult stretch in his NFL career, with the Deflategate controversy dominating headlines.

Article Title: Andy Murray’s wife Kim Sears and their four children: How family life has evolved since the former tennis champion retired from professional tennis and embraced fatherhood
Article Text:
Andy Murray and Kim Sears' combined net worth: Inside their journey from Grand Slam wins to business growth and family focus (Image Via Getty Images)

How Andy Murray enjoys family life after tennis retirement

Kim Sears’ background, artistic career and marriage to Andy Murray

How Andy Murray balances fatherhood and life beyond tennis

Andy Murray’s life changed dramatically when he retired from pro tennis at the 2024 Paris Olympics. The former British champion has adapted to a different lifestyle with wife Kim Sears and their four children following years of international travel, rigorous training schedules and big tournaments. Recent interviews have also shown how much he is enjoying the extra time at home after spending a good portion of his playing career away from his family.The couple have daughters, Sophia, Edie and Lola, and son, Teddy. Murray’s connection to tennis is still strong through his experience and continuing interest in the sport, but retirement has created more time for normal parenting and family activities. They also own Cromlix, the Scottish country-house hotel, which means the couple have a business interest in common beyond the tennis circuit.For Murray, retirement has been about showing up for the moments that were difficult to be present for consistently in his playing career. Professional tennis demanded long periods of travel between tournaments, training facilities and recovery sessions. Sometimes his family joined him on the tour, but inevitably the schedule curtailed the amount of unstructured time he could spend with his children.Murray said in a July 2026 interview that he liked retirement and having more time with his children.He admitted he’d been away a lot of his career and had missed his family often. The change has meant he can enjoy many of the routines that many parents take for granted, rather than family time dictated by an international competition calendar.The adjustment also demonstrates how the priorities of the couple have changed over time. Murray and Sears had children while he was still playing at the top level. Their eldest daughter Sophia was born in 2016, then Edie in 2017, Teddy in 2019 and their youngest daughter Lola in 2021. The children grew up during different stages of Murray's career, including times of injury, recovery and his eventual retirement.Family life now provides a different pace from the pressure of professional competition. Murray will be able to spend more time with his children and nurture their interests as they grow up. He has previously spoken of the importance of being a good father, making it clear that fatherhood is a priority separate from his sporting achievements.The change doesn't mean that tennis has disappeared from his life. Instead, it has changed its role in his daily routine. Murray’s schedule was shaped by years of matches and training, and he has had more freedom to pursue other interests, spend time with his family and consider opportunities related to the sport without the same pressure of competing on tour.Kim Sears has been in Murray’s life since they were teenagers. The pair first met at the US Open in 2005 when Sears was still at school, and Murray was on the way up in the professional game. Their relationship developed with his career, and the rigors of international competition were brought into their home. They tied the knot on 11 April 2015 at Scotland’s Dunblane Cathedral.Sears has tennis in his blood, too. Her father, Nigel Sears, is a former professional player and well-respected coach. Raised in the sport, she understands the demands it puts on you, though she has developed her own interests outside her husband’s career.Art is one of those hobbies. Sears is known for her portraiture and animal paintings, and she has maintained a fairly private public profile despite Murray’s international fame. Her creative work has also informed her involvement with Cromlix, shaping the interiors, artwork and overall atmosphere of the hotel.The couple bought a Victorian country house, Cromlix, near Dunblane in 2013. The property has a personal significance for Murray's family and a linkage to the local community. The couple have since turned the estate into a hospitality business, with Sears playing a key role in its creative direction since taking ownership. The hotel has therefore become a common project that unites family ties, design and business.From this, their partnership has grown beyond the public persona of a tennis champion and his wife. Sears has been there for Murray through the highs and lows of his playing career, but she has also continued to develop her own artistic interests and played an active role in the couple's business. Parenting is still a big part of life’s daily routine, but retirement has brought them a new avenue to share their time and responsibilities.Murray’s own approach to fatherhood has been influenced by his experience of raising children through a demanding professional career. The couple have largely kept their children away from too much public exposure, allowing them to grow up away from the constant attention that comes with their father’s sporting achievements.The family has still given glimpses of life together now and then. Previously, the comedian has talked about the ups and downs of being a parent, from taking part in activities his daughters pick to the realities of keeping children amused. He also discussed the strange opportunity of spending long periods of time at home during the COVID-19 lockdown, while admitting that lending a hand with children’s education could be a challenge.The obligations of professional life against domestic life are different now that he is no longer playing. Murray no longer has to structure his whole year around tournaments, travel and physiotherapy. This flexibility allows him to be more involved in his kids’ routines and to enjoy family experiences without needing to be away from home for extended periods.The family’s link to Cromlix means their private and professional lives are also intertwined. The hotel is more than just a business; it is part of the couple’s family history and relationship with Scotland. Their children visit the property, and the estate offers the family a connection between their current life and Murray’s roots in Dunblane. In an interview in June 2026, the couple talked about their family visits to Cromlix and what the property means to them personally.Murray’s life outside tennis is still being built, and his continuing relationship to the sport means retirement isn’t a total departure from the world that defined much of his adult life. But the emphasis has shifted. His family, his interests away from the court and the couple’s work at Cromlix now have more space to sit alongside his tennis legacy.For Murray and Sears, the next few years will mean new stages of parenthood as their children grow and develop their own interests. In their case, retirement isn’t so much about filling the void of major tennis triumphs as about clearing the decks for another kind of achievement: showing up for family life after years molded by the pro tour.Although Murray remains connected to tennis through his experience and ongoing interest in the sport, retirement has allowed him to place greater emphasis on fatherhood, family routines and the couple’s hospitality business. Their next chapter reflects a shift from the demands of elite competition towards family experiences and shared projects.
Article Summary: Andy Murray and Kim Sears married in April 2015. The couple have four children, including son Teddy. Murray retired from pro tennis at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Sears is an artist and owns Cromlix, a Scottish country-house hotel. Murray and Sears have been married since 2005.

Article Title: From $275 million to $325 million: How Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ soccer club grew in one year
Article Text:
Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 Million Soccer Investment (Getty Images)

Kansas City Current valuation rises from $275 million to $325 million

How the Mahomes family became KC Current owners

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations. That puts the club co-owned by Patrick and Brittany Mahomes second in the league, behind only Angel City FC at $340 million. A year ago Forbes had the Current at $275 million, so the value rose about 18 percent in twelve months.The numbers are simple. Forbes valued the Current at $275 million in 2025 and raised that to $325 million this spring. Angel City still leads, and its edge grew from $5 million last year to $15 million. Kansas City is still close enough that the top spot is not out of reach, though the gap moved the wrong way.Growth was not unique to Kansas City, and it was not even the fastest. Forbes says the average NWSL team, leaving out Denver and Boston in their debut seasons, is worth about $200 million, up 49 percent from last year. Angel City rose 21 percent. Bay FC, San Diego and Washington all grew faster than the Current's 18 percent, and the Spirit jumped 65 percent. Kansas City just started from a higher base, so each point of growth is worth more dollars.Stability explains part of it. The NWSL runs on a salary cap and has no relegation, so owners can plan years ahead instead of fearing a bad season will wreck the balance sheet.Investors pay for that kind of predictability, and each new expansion fee pushes the numbers higher.Revenue backs up the price. The list shows the KC Current at roughly $38 million, level with Angel City. Forbes says the club could climb out of operating losses as soon as this year. Red ink is not rare in pro sports. Twelve of 30 MLB teams and 16 of 29 MLS teams posted negative operating income in 2025.Brittany Mahomes played professional soccer in Iceland, and that background explains why the couple's name is on this club. She joined Angie and Chris Long in the ownership group, and Patrick came aboard in 2022, making him one of the first active NFL players with a stake in an NWSL team. Soccer is not his only side bet. He also owns pieces of the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City and Alpine F1.The club has kept its public message simple. Its statement reads: "When Angie Long, Chris Long, and Brittany Mahomes brought this NWSL franchise to Kansas City, they were clear in their commitment to do it right, for the players and for the city."Results on the field were less tidy when the list came out in April. Kansas City sat 14th under Armas, the first former MLS head coach to move into the NWSL, even after winning the 2025 Shield.Buyers are not waiting for a turnaround. Columbus will pay a $205 million expansion fee to join in 2028, while Denver paid $110 million in 2025. Against those numbers, $325 million for a club with a Shield and a purpose-built stadium looks less like a stretch.
Article Summary: The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations. That puts the club co-owned by Patrick and Brittany Mahomes second in the league. A year ago Forbes had the Current at $275 million, so the value rose about 18 percent in twelve months.

Article Title: 'It doesn't work like that': India coach keeps suspense over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's chances in playing XI

'Sanju is outstanding': Kotak backs openers

NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak has kept the suspense alive over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's chances of playing in the second T20I against New Zealand, insisting that the team management's selection decisions must be viewed in the larger interest of the side. With Ishan Kishan ruled out of Saturday's match due to injury, the 15-year-old batting sensation could be in contention, but Kotak backed current openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma.Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during India's four-wicket victory in the series opener. The BCCI medical team is monitoring his progress.Sooryavanshi, who has been on the sidelines since the Asian Games , is among the possible options as India prepare to face New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. However, Kotak stressed that selection cannot be driven by social media demands."...there is a lot of speculation in social media about the three openers. So, sometimes, social media should also appreciate that the team management calls are for the good of the team. Because, people want to play their own 11. It doesn't work like that," Kotak said on the eve of the second T20I.Kotak reserved special praise for Samson, who smashed 67 off 33 balls in the opening match, while Abhishek Sharma contributed 29 off just 12 deliveries.Their 93-run opening stand laid the foundation for India's successful chase of 226."Sanju is outstanding, he is a power-packed player. The way he approached the game yesterday. There are so many runs (to chase). If you ever put yourself in the place of a batsman and think that you have to hit three or four sixes in the first two overs, you will also be afraid of getting out."If you get out early in two or three games, you would think you would get dropped. So, overcoming all that and the intent (openers) they are showing, that excites me."Really, it is amazing that on top of power, talent and intent and everything, they are controlling their minds also. To get them into that fearless attitude, it is unbelievable," Kotak said.New Zealand posted 225/4 in the first T20I, with Glenn Phillips scoring an unbeaten 82 off 40 balls. India recovered from a brief middle-order wobble to complete the chase in 19.4 overs, with Shreyas Iyer making 42 and Naman Dhir remaining unbeaten on 42 off 15 balls.Kishan's absence leaves India with a selection decision ahead of the second match. Sooryavanshi's inclusion remains a possibility, but Kotak's comments underline the team's faith in Samson and Abhishek, whose fearless approach proved decisive in the series opener.
Article Summary: India coach Sitanshu Kotak backs current openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma. Ishan Kishan ruled out of Saturday's match due to injury. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be in contention to play in Christchurch. Kotak says selection cannot be driven by social media demands.

Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh continued her giant-killing run at the Silicon Valley Open 2026, producing a remarkable comeback to defeat Egypt's Salma Hany in a five-game thriller and book her maiden semi-final berth at a PSA Gold-level event. The 18-year-old World No. 15 recovered from a 1-2 deficit to register a 4-11, 11-8, 4-11, 11-2, 11-5 victory over the sixth-seeded Egyptian in 42 minutes in Redwood City, California.Anahat showed tremendous resilience after twice falling behind in the contest, raising her level in the final two games to complete an impressive turnaround. Having conceded the opening and third games, the Indian dominated the closing stages, dropping just seven points across the last two games to seal a landmark win.The victory marks another significant milestone in Anahat's burgeoning career and comes on the back of her stunning second-round upset of eight-time world champion and World No. 3 Nour ElSherbini.Hany made a strong start, capitalising on Anahat's errors to take the opening game 11-4. The Indian responded with an improved performance in the second, winning it 11-8 to restore parity.However, the Egyptian regained control in the third game, cruising to another 11-4 win to move within a game of victory.With her quarter-final hopes hanging in the balance, Anahat produced a superb response, stepping up her intensity to dismantle Hany 11-2 in the fourth game.The teenager carried that momentum into the decider, maintaining her composure and dictating the rallies to close out the contest 11-5. Her emphatic finish underlined her ability to respond under pressure against an experienced opponent.The win ensures Anahat reaches the last four of a PSA Gold event for the first time in her career, further strengthening her growing reputation on the international squash circuit.Anahat's reward for the hard-fought quarter-final victory is a semi-final showdown against Malaysia's World No. 4 Sivasangari Subramaniam, who booked her place in the last four with a straight-games win over compatriot Rachel Arnold.The clash will renew a rivalry established at the 2026 Asian Games, where Sivasangari defeated Anahat 3-0 in the women's singles final to claim gold, leaving the Indian with silver. Anahat had made history at the continental event by becoming the first Indian woman to reach the squash singles final.Anahat has enjoyed an impressive campaign in Redwood City. She began by defeating Egypt's Nour Aboulmakarim 11-8, 11-8, 12-10 in the opening round before producing one of the biggest wins of her career against ElSherbini, beating the top-tier Egyptian 11-8, 11-8, 11-7.

India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has stressed the importance of trusting his process and staying focused on his game despite the criticism and opinions that come with playing for the national team. His comments came after India chased down 230/6 with two balls remaining to record their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the opening match of the five-game series.Samson said he does not play to silence critics. Instead, he focuses on his preparation, keeps things simple and avoids letting social media reactions affect his mindset.“To be very honest, you can’t focus on what people on social media or others are saying. You have to stay committed to the process and create the right environment for yourself. Playing for Indian cricket is not easy, with so much noise and so many people having their own opinions. But I don’t play this game with the mindset of proving anyone wrong. I keep my cricket at the forefront, trust my process, respect my practice and focus on doing the best I can. I like to keep things simple and stay focused on what I can control, rather than letting outside opinions influence my mindset,” Samson told reporters after the match.Samson played a key role in the chase, scoring 67 off 33 balls to give India a strong start. However, a middle-order collapse put the team under pressure before Naman Dhir struck an unbeaten 42 off just 15 deliveries to seal the victory.Samson credited India's attacking approach across the powerplay, middle overs and final overs for helping the team achieve the record chase. He said the team has continued to back this style of cricket since winning the 2024 T20 World Cup.“We approach the powerplay, middle overs and death overs very differently. Even when chasing 170, if we get off to a flying start, we make sure we try to finish the game in the powerplay itself. That’s something we’ve been doing really well over the last couple of years,” Samson said.He added that India must continue trusting their approach, even when it does not always produce the desired results.Samson said the team's priority is to build on what works, play to their strengths and put the team's interests first. India's four-wicket win gives them a 1-0 lead in the five-match series, with the second T20I next on the schedule.

Article Title: Against the odds, Sheetal Devi reigns supreme with double gold at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Archer Sheetal Devi (File Photo/ AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The tears came first, the smiles followed. As Sheetal Devi stood victorious once again, the emotions of a remarkable journey spilled over at the Okazaki Central Park Multipurpose Square in Nagoya — the venue for para-archery competitions. They were tears of overcoming adversity, of keeping promises made to herself, her family and coaches, and of seeing a year of relentless hard work culminate in gold. The archer had done it again, returning from the Asian Para Games with two gold medals and a silver.The 19-year-old from J&K’s Loidhar village in Kishtwar district produced a stunning double gold performance on Thursday, retaining her women’s compound individual crown before teaming up with Toman Kumar to clinch the mixed team title. She had already won silver in the women’s compound doubles alongside quadruple amputee Payal Nag on Tuesday.The individual final against Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah was a test of nerve. Trailing 55-59 after the opening two ends, Sheetal faced a four-point deficit against the 41-year-old Singaporean. But the world No. 1 responded with six 10s, including three arrows landing closest to the bull’s-eye, turning the contest around to lead by two points.With gold within reach, she shot three 9s in the final end. Alim needed a strong finish but managed only 26 points to Sheetal’s 27, handing the Indian a 142-139 a second successive individual gold.Earlier, Sheetal and Toman had beaten Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148. After establishing a four-point advantage midway through the final, the Indians absorbed Indonesia’s late challenge and held on for gold.Their combined qualification score of 1,402 had also set a world record. “There was some pressure because of the wind. But my coach told me not to worry and just reset for the next end,” she said after her win. “The silver was also good for me. But the gold I won today, I am happy that what I had set to do, I have done,” she added.Born without arms, Sheetal positions her bow with her feet and legs, drawing and releasing the string with her shoulder and jaw. From winning gold at Hangzhou in 2023 to claiming bronze at the Paris Paralympics, her rise has been extraordinary.India celebrated another medal as Swati Chaudhary won the country’s first-ever W1 archery medal, taking silver after losing 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan. Swati had led 4-2 before Cen fought back to win.
Article Summary: Sheetal Devi wins two gold medals and a silver at the Asian Para Games. The 19-year-old from J&K's Loidhar village in Kishtwar district produced a stunning double gold performance on Thursday. She retained her women’s compound individual crown before teaming up with Toman Kumar to clinch the mixed team title.

The Indian para shooter produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, setting a new World Record and Asian Para Games Record.Mona's latest triumph came after she had already struck gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.Mona delivered a composed performance in the 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final to secure the gold medal with a world-record score of 357.5. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara , narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Mona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Mona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.
Article Summary: India's Mona Agarwal wins second gold of 2026 Asian Para Games. She produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang. India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara, narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth.

Article Title: Injured Ishan Kishan ruled out of 2nd T20I, paves way for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's return to playing XI
Article Text:

Samson, Abhishek lead India's record chase

India's teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could get another opportunity in the playing XI after wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan was ruled out of the second T20I against New Zealand with a low-grade right adductor strain. The injury has opened up a selection question for India ahead of Saturday's encounter at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, with the team management weighing its options after a record-breaking chase in the series opener.The Board of Control for Cricket in India BCCI ) confirmed that Kishan sustained the injury during the first T20I. The BCCI medical team is monitoring his progress, but the wicketkeeper-batter will miss the second match as India look to extend their 1-0 lead in the five-match series.Sooryavanshi, who was part of India's squad but missed the opening match, is among the possible options to replace Kishan. The 15-year-old has already made his senior international debut and represented India at the 2026 Asian Games, where he was part of the gold-medal-winning men's cricket team. His inclusion against New Zealand would therefore mark a return to the playing XI.New Zealand posted 225/4 after being asked to bat first, with Glenn Phillips leading the charge through an unbeaten 82 off 40 balls.Finn Allen contributed 45 off 24 deliveries, while Bevon Jacobs added a brisk 31 off 16 as the hosts built a formidable total.India responded with an explosive opening partnership between Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma. Samson smashed 67 off 33 balls, while Abhishek contributed 29 off 12, helping India race to 93 without loss before the first wicket fell.The momentum briefly shifted when India lost three wickets in quick succession, slipping to 122/4. Captain Shreyas Iyer then scored a valuable 42 off 28 balls to steady the chase, while Axar Patel added 24. Naman Dhir eventually delivered the decisive blow, remaining unbeaten on 42 off just 15 balls to guide India home with two deliveries to spare.

Sooryavanshi, who was part of India's squad but missed the opening match, is among the possible options.

Article Title: Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan Vadra's photos of protest taken down by Bikaner House
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra, an artist, faced issues at Bikaner House regarding his exhibition's protest images





NEW DELHI: Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, has alleged that the Bikaner House administration removed several photographs documenting recent protests and youth movements in India, just hours before the opening of his solo exhibition.Titled No Idea is Final, the exhibition was previewed on Wednesday and is scheduled to open on Thursday.Speaking to news agency PTI, Raihan said the administration gave him a deadline to remove the photographs, warning that the exhibition would otherwise be cancelled.“They told us at 3.30 pm today if the images are not taken down by 5 pm, the show will be cancelled. They said it is not the right time for such photos to be shown,” he said.Raihan also alleged that an image of the national flag was taken down by the administration, but he subsequently put it back.In a statement shared with PTI, Raihan said the exhibition featured a mix of wildlife photography, abstract works and street photography documenting recent youth movements in India.He said the Bikaner House management had first contacted him at 6 pm on Tuesday, raising objections to what it described as the “political nature” of the protest photographs and asking him to remove them.Raihan objected to the timing of the request, saying he had shared the exhibition’s detailed proposal and layout with the management well in advance.“I made it clear that in view of the fact that I had shared the detailed proposal and layout of the show well in advance with the Bikaner House management it was incorrect on their part to request the removal of 50% of the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening,” he said.The Bikaner House administration was not immediately available for comment on the allegations.
Article Summary: Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert, faced issues at Bikaner House regarding his exhibition's protest images. The exhibition featured a mix of wildlife photography, abstract works and street photography documenting recent youth movements in India.

Article Title: CJP activists’ detention puts spotlight on how SEMs play a crucial role
Article Text:
Recent observations by the Delhi HC have scrutinized the actions of these magistrates concerning the detainment of CJP activists

Who are SEMs?

How are they different from judicial magistrates?

When can an SEM ask someone to furnish a peace bond ?

Procedure: Under Section 130, the magistrate must issue a written order explaining the basis for the proceedings, the proposed bond amount, its duration and the number of sureties required.

Duration: A peace bond can be required for up to one year, and the amount must not be excessive.

Can it be challenged? The person must be given an opportunity to explain why they should not be required to furnish the bond. The magistrate then conducts an inquiry under Section 135.

When can an SEM order detention?

During inquiry: Under Section 135(3), an SEM may require immediate security if necessary to prevent a breach of peace or danger to public safety. If the person fails to furnish it, they may be detained until the inquiry concludes.

After inquiry: Under Section 136, the magistrate can order security if the inquiry establishes it is necessary. Under Section 137, the person must be discharged if the need for security isn’t established.

Failure to furnish security: Section 141 provides for imprisonment in specified circumstances, including failure to furnish security after a final order or breach of a qualifying bond.

Who can stand as a surety?

“Photograph mismatch”: The first surety’s photograph on the bond allegedly didn’t match his Aadhaar

“Insufficient identity proof”: He reportedly failed to produce another valid ID and gave unsatisfactory answers during questioning

“Lack of basic details”: The second surety couldn’t provide basic information, including the parentage and address of Saurav Das, for whom she stood as surety

“Insufficient control”: The SEM concluded the sureties didn’t have sufficient control over the activists to ensure their presence when required





NEW DELHI: Though a common feature in cases involving summary or preventive detention by police, the powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests rocking Delhi are released or remain behind bars.A person not familiar with the rare, overlapping functions and powers of the executive and judiciary may conclude SEMs are a rung of the judiciary where a person picked up by police is produced within 24 hours.However, the reality is more complex, since the law empowers govt officials, mostly police officers, to exercise magisterial powers in cases of detention, where they can even remand a detainee to judicial custody, as happened in the case of CJP’s Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea. The court, however, refused to go into merits.Under Section 15 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), state govts can appoint executive magistrates or police officers of at least superintendent of police rank as SEMs for specific areas, periods or duties.Depending on state-specific notifications, these officers can also be deputy collectors or tehsildars or senior police officers of ACP rank.Their primary role is to take preventive measures to maintain public order and stop anticipated breaches of peace.Under BNSS Section 9, the state govt establishes courts of judicial magistrates in consultation with HC, which appoints their presiding officers. Judicial magistrates deal with criminal cases and trials while SEMs exercise executive powers, including initiating preventive proceedings.SEMs cannot conduct criminal trials or convict people through these proceedings, but are authorised to release or grant police or judicial remand. Under the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), the corresponding provision for SEMs was Section 21.Under Section 126, an SEM can initiate proceedings if there is sufficient ground to believe a person is likely to breach the peace or disturb public tranquillity.Separately, Section 163 allows an executive magistrate to issue urgent orders to prevent specified dangers or disturbances, including restricting public gatherings when legal conditions are met.Detention is not automatic once proceedings begin.A surety undertakes responsibility under a bond to help ensure the person concerned meets its conditions. Under Section 140, an SEM can reject a surety found unfit, but must conduct an inquiry, give the parties a reasonable opportunity to be heard and record reasons in writing.In Das and Ranka’s case, the SEM rejected fresh sureties over reported “discrepancies” in identification documents and missing details.
Article Summary: The powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests are released or remain behind bars. Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea.

Article Title: 'I clean, they dirty faster': MP's Bittu Tabahi may quit cleaning river forever
Article Text:
Photo: @bittu_tabahi/ Instagram

Bittu cleaned river stretch alone, larger civic failure is now making him fight losing battle





BHOPAL: Madhya Pradesh's 20-year-old college student Surendra Singh Choudhary-better known to the country as "Bittu Tabahi"-is a dejected man. Bittu, who hogged international limelight for single-handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora, says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it-sometimes almost immediately. The situation worsened after Dussehra, when fresh waste accumulated along the banks he had worked so hard to restore."I have been working to clean this river for the past year. Every time I have cleaned it, people have dirtied it again," he said, his voice heavy with disappointment. "I am starting to lose heart.""I think I should focus on my studies," Bittu said.I don't believe I will be able to continue cleaning the Ajnar river any longer."The statement marks a troubling turn for a campaign that became a symbol of individual environmental action. Bittu's central argument remains simple: removing garbage is only temporary if people continue to throw waste into the river. Lasting change, he believes, requires citizens to stop littering in the first place.Ajnar, which flows through Biaora in Rajgarh district, had long been treated as an open dumping ground.Passers-by reportedly covered their mouths with cloth to escape its stench. Bittu began cleaning a stretch of the river on Jan 26, initially with a few friends, but soon found himself working alone, armed with little more than basic tools and determination.There was no govt order, no funding and no formal campaign behind his effort. He used his own money for supplies, entered foul water despite not knowing how to swim, and removed waste bag by bag. For a while, the results were visible. The stretch Bittu cleaned became noticeably clearer, and his videos earned praise from across India and abroad.But that recognition has not stopped the river from being littered again. His frustration deepened after he installed two dustbins along the riverbank, hoping residents and visitors would dispose of waste responsibly. One of the bins later went missing. Bittu clarified that the dustbins were meant for public use, not personal convenience.During another clean-up, conducted with the local Nagar Palika team, Bittu found an Indian national flag among the waste. He used the moment to ask a question that has become central to his campaign: "When will we understand our responsibility?"Those who have followed Bittu's work describe a young volunteer whose energy was once extraordinary. He cleaned without machinery, faced health risks and snake encounters, and continued even after criticism. But repeated relapse of pollution has begun to test that resolve. Bittu's exhaustion highlights a larger civic failure. A single student can clean a river, but he cannot police a town's habits, provide permanent waste infra, or sustain a clean-up alone.
Article Summary: Surendra Singh Choudhary, known as "Bittu Tabahi," is a 20-year-old college student from Madhya Pradesh. Bittu hogged international limelight for single- handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora. He says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it.

Article Title: Cheered in Chhota Udepur, but Vadodara shuts stage to Muslim who played Lakshmana for 14 years
Article Text:
Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion.





VADODARA: On Dussehra , Abid Sheikh drew applause in tribal Chhota Udepur for bringing the characters of Kevat and Meghnad alive on stage in a Ram Leela.In Vadodara, however, the city he calls home, the 39-year-old was unable to perform in the Ram Leela he had been associated with for nearly 14 years, after objections to his participation over his religion by right-wing groups.The contrast has left Sheikh, a science graduate who grew up fascinated by the Ramayana, grappling with an unexpected rejection from a tradition that had become an integral part of his life.For years, Sheikh played Laxman and Bharat in the Ram Leela organised by the North India Cultural Association (NICA) at Polo Ground during Dussehra. He learnt his dialogues, rehearsed for weeks and earned appreciation from audiences. His family, too, shared his commitment, giving up non-vegetarian food during the rehearsal period until the festival concluded.But the welcome he had long received on stage in Vadodara changed last year when some right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim.“I played different roles in Ram Leela for around 14 years and was showered with love and appreciation by the audience.Last year, some activists suddenly turned up during rehearsals and objected to my casting because of my religion. I was shocked, as I never expected this,” Sheikh told TOI.He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him. This year, he was not invited to perform in the Vadodara production.“Ram Leela had become a part of my life, but they did not want me anywhere near the stage,” he said.The rejection was particularly painful because his association with the epic began in childhood. After watching a cartoon based on the Ramayana, Sheikh developed a fascination for Laxman. An opportunity to perform in a school Ram Leela gave him his first taste of acting, and he continued playing characters from the epic for years.Shashikant Das, director, NICA, told TOI: “Sheikh is such a good actor and he is an ardent fan of Ramayan. He chants Hanuman Chalisa. But Bajrang Dal activists came last year and protested against his role. I argued and fought in Sheikh’s defence.”“But the management came under pressure. So, this time he wasn’t invited for the Ram Leela. It’s sad that we lost a good actor like him,” Das said and pointed out that those preparing the giant effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna at Polo Ground are also Muslim artists from Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion. Right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim. He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him.
